text:
pagerduty-bot: PAGER: High GPU queue depth detected in prod-gpu-pool-east. Trigger: autoscaler failed to add nodes; sustained queue growth > 95th percentile for 4m. Sev2 page to oncall.

alex: I'm seeing queue length spike on the runtime dashboards, latency climbing. Canary traffic showing 500s from runtime.

sam: Confirmed. Autoscaler logs show repeated failures: quota_exceeded + internal driver errors across a subset of nodes.

irene: @oncall are you able to take? I'm seeing CUDA Xid 63 and OOMs on a few nodes, kernel logs attached in infra-bot.

oncall: I'm on it. Paging into rotation; will patch here. First glance: multiple nodes flapping between Ready/NotReady, some with nvml resets.

luis: Customer impact: a handful of paid customers reported timeouts for batch embeddings and streaming responses. CS has one open high-priority ticket.

sam: Autoscaler attempted 12 scale-out operations in last 10m, 9 failed with "insufficient capacity" and 3 aborted because driver reports Xid on init.

infra-bot: Node events:
```
node-rt-7f2: kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:03:00): 63
node-rt-9a1: systemd: docker: container OOM killed
node-rt-3c4: kubelet: NodeNotReady: NetworkPluginNotReady
```

alex: That Xid 63 is the GPU page fault/driver crash. If those nodes are flapping autoscaler thinks capacity isn't useable and won't attach pods.

irene: I'm dumping dmesg and nvidia-smi output to /tmp. Suspect a driver regression from last week's hotpatch.

sam: For immediate mitigation, we can: 1) mark flapping nodes as unschedulable and cordon; 2) force a fallback routing to cpu/quantized small-model pool for affected routes; 3) raise autoscaler soft limit temporarily to allow additional smaller-instance launch. Thoughts?

oncall: Do 1 and 2 immediately. Cordoning now: `kubectl cordon node-rt-7f2` -> cordoned. Cordon node-rt-9a1 and node-rt-3c4.

alex: Routing change: updating route table to divert low-priority streaming to fallback-models cluster. Patch applied via router: `curl -X POST https://router.internal/route-swap -d '{"route":"/stream","pool":"fallback-small-gpu"}'`

infra-bot: Router responded 200. Verified 95% of stream traffic rerouted.

luis: Notifying impacted customers: CS posted an update with ETA 30m for mitigation and recommended temporary workarounds (reduce concurrency, switch to embeddings-lite).

sam: While cordoning, I also triggered node drain on the flapping nodes. Some pods stuck in Terminating due to model checkpoint write on local /tmp. Adding `--force --grace-period=30` to get drains moving.

irene: I'm rolling back the driver hotpatch on a spare node to validate. Installing earlier driver v525.60.13 on node-rt-4b8 for test.

oncall: Test node with older driver booted cleanly, no Xid logs after 6m of load. Good signal.

alex: Can we taint the older-driver nodes to accept critical workloads only, then scale a tiny set of pools to them while we patch the fleet?

sam: Yes. Plan: carve out 4 nodes with stable driver, create a temporary dedicated pool for high-priority customers, update policy to route their gen requests there. That reduces overall queue pressure.

infra-bot: Autoscaler note: Manual override applied: max_nodes increased from 150 -> 180 for prod-gpu-pool-east (temporary). API key: auto-override-330123.

alex: After overrides and reroutes, queue length trending down from 1200 -> 240 in 12 minutes. Token latency also dropping.

luis: CS updated customers. One enterprise customer requested SLA credit; I'm escalating to AR team.

oncall: We're still seeing ~2 nodes with repeated OOMs on pod startup. I've isolated one container that keeps hitting kernel OOM because the model loader allocates pinned memory without fallback. I'll push a quick hotfix to the runtime image that adds a soft-fallback to quantized load when pinned alloc fails.

irene: Hotfix pushed as runtime:v2026.3-hotfix-alloc. Rolling to drained nodes first.

infra-bot: Deployment rollout: runtime -> canary group 5 nodes -> success. Monitoring.

sam: Canary runtime passed smoke tests; rolling to the 4 stable-driver nodes next.

alex: After rollout, we see OOM count drop to zero on those nodes. Autoscaler now successfully provisioning 8 additional nodes to replace cordoned ones.

oncall: I'll keep the cordoned nodes cordoned and schedule a maintenance window to repro driver on a staging cluster. Ops will coordinate kernel logs and escalate to vendor if driver bug confirmed.

luis: Summary for customers: mitigation applied (traffic reroute + temporary pool + autoscaler override + runtime hotfix). Estimated full recovery in 45m.

sam: Post-incident actions: 1) Revert autoscaler override after stable; 2) Fleet driver validation gate on hotpatches; 3) Add model-loader alloc fallback test to CI; 4) Improve autoscaler logic to ignore nodes that report Xid within the boot window for 10m.

alex: Also add a dashboard alarm that correlates Xid rate + failed scaleouts to trigger a preemptive route diversion.

infra-bot: Incident annotated: incident_id=INC-3301, started=3301234567, severity=sev2, mitigations=[cordon_nodes, route_reroute, autoscaler_override, runtime_hotfix].

customer-success: Noted. CS will draft an RCA update for clients once postmortem is ready.

oncall: Leaving this thread open for a follow-up postmortem. Handing back to platform rotation. Good work team. :thumbsup:

alex: Oncall handoff acknowledged. I'll create the postmortem ticket and link logs.

sam: Logs and snippets saved to: https://logs.redwood.internal/3301234567/ (permissioned).

irene: Will follow up with driver vendor if we confirm regression.

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-3301 moved to status: mitigated -> monitoring.
